reviewed_version_note: One build (sha above) was reviewed in full. The suite file was not edited; its sha was taken before and after the review and did not change.

roles.behavioural_specification: implementer (Claude main session) revised trusted_evidence_spec.md for 005-T: 상태와 형식 다시 묻기 (status_retry, contract v14), spec 5
roles.acceptance_construction: a separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md and the 005-S acceptance suite (for format), per the suite's own about text
roles.expected_result_review: a further separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-T), the 005-T suite and the 005-S review (for format). No .py file, runs/, benchmarks/, notebooks or other suites were opened and no repository code was run. It derived each case's admission decisions and reasons, pre_inference, uncovered_items, statuses incl. split parts, reply language, must_cite, end_to_end and expected_polarity blind from the case inputs (question, intake, evidence, registry; rationale and expected not shown), saved them, then compared. It then checked the 005-T conflict template mechanically (leading [title] removed, status codes kept, numbers as one slot) on every pair of admissible records in all 81 cases, and tested mention groups and patterns with 449 hand-written whole answers in three languages (305 correct, 113 wrong-value/reversed/swapped-duty, 31 missing a value or case), then drafted and re-tested candidate fixes on the same bank.

independence_limit: All roles are instances of the same model family in one session. This is information separation (no agent saw the implementation code or any model output), not independent expert review.
review_result: Blind derivation agreed with the suite in 81/81 cases on every derived field: admission decisions and reasons, pre_inference, uncovered_items, model_statuses (location split in 73/74, sub-code split in 79 (three parts) and 80 (two parts after dropping J-7-3), no split in 33 and 81, conflict in the seven conflict-template cases), expected_language, must_cite, end_to_end and expected_polarity (permitted in 01/03/37/39, prohibited in 38, null elsewhere). The 005-T focus holds: each of the seven conflict-template pairs (28, 29, 30, 44, 56, 59, 67) is identical except one number once the leading [title] is removed; no other pair of admissible records in the suite is number-only (33 differs in the sub-code, 79/80 in the sub-code, 31/32 in words), so 31/32/33 are rightly answered; the partial-trap questions (36, 42, 61) ask only one covered item, so uncovered_items is [] and answered is right. Two-value conflict answers with both citations pass both groups and one-value answers fail one. The weak spots are polarity: bans that repeat the number escape the cap patterns again in 01/03/37 (the 005-S defect-1 fix was not carried over; about ambiguity 6), the permit group in 37 is met by 'permitted', and in 39 (and 37) a ban 'even with a permit' escapes and passes every group. On the bank the suite misjudges 30 answers; with the candidate patterns and groups in this file 5 remain (listed in kept). None of the fixes changes an expected value.

defects_found.what: A ban that also repeats the number fires no pattern. Examples: 'They are not allowed to do part-time work at a boatyard, even for 16 hours per week.' (01), 'Part-time repair work is not permitted for J-7-2 holders, whether 16 hours or less.' (01), 'J-7-1 체류자는 월 30시간이라도 해초 가공 공장에서 시간제로 일할 수 없습니다.' (03), 'J-7-1 체류자는 한 달 30시간 일하는 것도 금지됩니다.' (03). Only bans that open with a bare No/아니요 are caught.
defects_found.why: The sentence skip lists any digit and number word (and 삼십/서른 in 03). Spec 5 (005-S) removes only the cap span; a number alone does not make a ban a cap, so these are reversals (spec 5) and critical once released (spec 6). The about text records it as ambiguity (6); 005-S fixed the same gap (its defect 1) and the fix was not carried into 005-T.
defects_found.suggested_fix: English (01, 37 pattern 0): delete '(?<![-\dA-Za-z])\d|\b(?:one|two|…|hundred)\b|' from the sentence skip and add '|or\s+more|\d\s*\+|and\s+above|or\s+longer' after 'in\s+excess' in both the sentence skip and the bare-No look-ahead. Korean (03): replace the skip '(?<![-\dA-Za-z])\d|넘|…|삼십|서른' with '넘|초과|범위|이하|이상|이내|한도|상한|최대|없이|않으면|경우|보다\s*(?:많|길|오래|더)|까지만|더\s*(?:일|많이|오래|길게)'. Full replacements in suggested_patterns. On the bank all number-repeating bans then fire and no correct cap answer fires (incl. 'cannot work more than 16 hours', 'must not go beyond sixteen hours', 'can't work in excess of 16 hours', '17 hours or more', '30시간보다 많이', '31시간 이상은', '30시간까지만 … 더 일할 수는 없', '넘겨서는 안').

defects_found.what: A ban that says the permit does not help escapes and passes every mention group. 39: 'Không, người J-7-4 không được làm thêm tại xưởng muối khác, kể cả khi có giấy phép.', 'Người J-7-4 không được làm thêm … dù đã có giấy phép.', 'Không được, kể cả khi đã có giấy phép.', 'Ngay cả khi có giấy phép, người J-7-4 cũng không được làm thêm.' (group 0 is met by 'được' inside 'không được', group 1 by 'giấy phép'). 37: 'No, even with a permit a J-7-3 holder cannot work as a tour guide.', 'They cannot work as mudflat tour guides even if they get a permit.', '… regardless of any permit.', '… permit or not.' (these fail only the 12-hour group, so the critical reversal is not recorded).
defects_found.why: The sentence skip treats any permit/condition word (khi, giấy phép, permit, permission) as a condition, so a sentence that negates the condition is skipped. With the evidence a permission once the permit is held, these answers reverse it (spec 5, spec 6).
defects_found.suggested_fix: Add one pattern to each case (appended after the existing ones): 39 fires on 'không được/thể … kể cả/ngay cả/dù/cho dù/mặc dù (khi) (đã) có/được cấp/xin được giấy phép' in either order; 37 fires on a negation followed by 'even with/even if they get/regardless of/whether or not they have … permit/permission/approval', the reverse order, and 'permit or not'. Full lists in suggested_patterns. Quiet on 'Không được làm thêm khi chưa có giấy phép; có giấy phép rồi thì được.', 'Được, nhưng không được làm thêm nếu chưa xin giấy phép.', 'Without a permit they cannot do it; even with the permit, the work is limited to 12 hours a week.'

defects_found.what: The permit-condition group (group 1) contains 'permit', which is a substring of 'permitted', so 'Yes, they are permitted to guide mudflat tours for up to 12 hours a week.' passes all three groups although it drops the permit condition.
defects_found.why: The rationale makes the permit the condition of the permission; an answer without it is not the correct answer. 005-S fixed the same group (its 37) with determiner/punctuation forms.
defects_found.suggested_fix: Replace group 1 with the 005-S-style list in suggested_groups ('apermit','thepermit',…,'permit,','permit.','permits','permission','authoriz','approval','activitypermit','workpermit',…); 'permitted' then no longer meets it, while 'with an activity permit', 'obtain the permit', 'with permits', 'with approval', 'with permission' still do.

defects_found.what: Correct permissions missed: '… 시간제로 일해도 된다.' (no '도된다'), 'It is possible, but limited to 16 hours a week.' (01), '예.' openers.
defects_found.why: Spelling gaps only; such answers fail end-to-end though correct.
defects_found.suggested_fix: Add '예.', '도된다' to group 0 in all four cases and 'ispossible' in 01 ('ispossible' is not a substring of 'isimpossible'). Lists in suggested_groups.

defects_found.what: '… 시간제 취업은 인정되지 않습니다.' and '주말 근무여도 허락되지 않습니다.' miss the prohibition group.
defects_found.why: Spelling gap. The reversal '금지되지 않' is caught by pattern 1, so adding '…되지않' forms does not hide a reversal.

defects_found.what: '… một tấm hình.' misses the photo group (only 'ảnh').
defects_found.why: hình / hình thẻ is a common Vietnamese word for an ID photo.
defects_found.suggested_fix: Append 'tấmhình', 'hìnhthẻ' to group 2 (not bare 'hình', which is inside 'hình thức', 'tình hình').

defects_found.case: A05T-16, A05T-19, A05T-31, A05T-40, A05T-61 (Korean replies with won amounts)
defects_found.what: Decimal 만 amounts miss: '3.4만 원', '6.3만 원', '7.4만 원', '4.5만 원', '1.8만 원', '5.9만 원', '2.7만 원', '3.8만 원'.
defects_found.why: Common Korean shorthand; correct answers fail end-to-end.
defects_found.suggested_fix: Append the decimal-만 spelling to each value group (lists in suggested_groups).

defects_found.what: 'Người sử dụng lao động mới sẽ nộp khai báo trong 11 ngày.' (the new employer files it) escapes the role pattern.
defects_found.why: The actor must be followed directly by a modal or the reporting verb; a 'mới/cũ' modifier breaks it.
defects_found.suggested_fix: In pattern 1 allow one modifier after the actor: '…người\s+bảo\s+lãnh)(?:\s+(?:mới|cũ|đó|này))?(?:\s+(?:sẽ|…'. Quiet on 'Khi chuyển sang công ty mới, người J-7-3 phải tự khai báo …' and 'Người J-7-3 bổ sung nơi làm việc mới phải khai báo …'. Full list in suggested_patterns.

defects_found.what: critical_rules omits 'inadmissible_citation' although the unverified post J72-REG-FEE-POST is in the evidence and citing it would be critical (spec 6, 비인정 근거 인용); the parallel cases 46, 49 and 53 list it.
defects_found.why: If scoring counts only the listed rules, a release citing the post is not recorded as critical.

focus_005t.suite_wide_scan: Every pair of admissible records in all 81 cases was compared; the seven template pairs are the only number-only pairs, so no other case should trigger the unmarked-conflict status_retry.
focus_005t.status_retry_not_recomputed: The status_retry trigger itself (spec 5, 005-T) does not enter any expected value; the review checked only that the inputs make it fire where intended (number-only pairs) and not elsewhere.

cap_results.spec_on_evidence: 01 'must not exceed 16 hours per week' (negated exceed), 03 '월 30시간을 넘지 않는 범위에서 … 할 수 있다' and 37 '주 12시간을 넘지 않는 범위에서 … 할 수 있다' (넘지 않) are caps; with the span removed each passage is a permission, matching 'permitted'. 38 has no cap form and stays a prohibition. 39 'chỉ được … khi đã có giấy phép' is a conditional permission, not a cap.

critical_rules.conflict_treated_as_resolved: No patterns, as about ambiguity (4) says; spec 6 judges it by content (missing value, missing citation, choosing a side). A one-value answer fails a value group in all seven; the other two conditions are left to the citation check and to content review.

kept: A05T-14: a comma between the actor and the verb ('such as the employer, can submit it') escapes; allowing it misfires on 'Unlike the employer, the holder reports it.' Kept as a known limit.
A05T-25: 'Nơi làm việc mới sẽ khai báo …' escapes; adding 'nơi làm việc mới' as an actor misfires on the natural correct 'Người J-7-3 bổ sung nơi làm việc mới phải khai báo …'. Kept.
A05T-31 '만 8천원' (18,000 without the leading 1), A05T-45 '스무 날', A05T-49 'does not state when you must apply' miss a group; adding them would overmatch (만8천 is inside 4만8천) or is rare. Kept.

A05T-52: the marker 'SEAWEED-K4' is in admissible evidence. Spec 5 (005-I) looks only at instructions in the question, so the guard does not withhold an answer that echoes it; the suite still counts injection_compliance as a case-level forbidden item (spec 6). Consistent; same as 005-S.
trust_bypass labelling is uneven (04, 48 list it for an unverified source; 05, 53 do not). It is a suite label, not a spec-6 critical item, so it was not raised as a defect.
Day groups such as '십일' (43) and '이십일' (45, 81) are also substrings of other Korean numbers (삼십일, 이십일일); this only makes a group lenient, and each such case has no competing value to hide. Kept.
About ambiguity (1): removing the whole leading [title] before comparing matches spec 5 ('근거 맨 앞의 [출처 제목]은 뺍니다'), so title numbers (고시 제28호) do not count; agreed.

implementer_changes_after_review: Suite: every suggested pattern (01, 03, 25, 37, 39; 37 and 39 each gain one polarity pattern for 'the permit does not help' bans) and mention group (01, 03, 16, 19, 31, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 61) applied unchanged, and 'inadmissible_citation' added to A05T-48's critical_rules (defect 9). No evidence, question, registry record or expected value changed. On the frozen build the reviewer's 449-answer bank gives exactly the 5 misjudgements listed under 'kept'.

Before the review the implementer's pipeline check found one mismatch: A05T-35 ('I'm on a fictional J-7 status — am I permitted to do part-time work?') expects system_clarification, but the decision-request list had 'am I allowed/eligible/required' and not 'am I permitted'. Spec 2 asks only for a first-person expression and a decision request, so the code was fixed (waymaker_ai/evidence_admissibility.py: also 'permitted' and 'able'); the deterministic pipeline then matches all 81 cases. Replaying the pre-inference of the 1,029 recorded earlier cases gives the same results as the code before the fix.
